descriptors.concept_name: Classes and Administrative Structure of Income-Tax Authorities
descriptors.definition: The Income-tax Act establishes a hierarchical administrative machinery headed by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, followed by various classes of directors-general, chief commissioners, commissioners, and subordinate officers. The CBDT functions under the Ministry of Finance to exercise statutory control, supervise the department, and frame necessary rules for proper administration.
inclusion: Assessing Officers including ACIT, DCIT, and authorized ITOs
exclusion: Judicial courts outside the income-tax department hierarchy
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from appellate dispute resolution panels and general civil courts by operating purely within the direct tax administrative machinery.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax authorities must exercise their statutory powers and perform assigned functions in accordance with the regulatory directions issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes. The CBDT distributes and regulates these administrative authorities based on criteria including territorial area, classes of persons, types of incomes, or specific cases.
inclusion: General or special orders assigning officer jurisdiction
Higher authorities exercising powers of lower authorities under board direction
Delegation of assessment functions to additional or joint commissioners
exclusion: Self-assigned jurisdiction by officers without specific board authorization or statutory backing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general administrative powers because it specifically governs the territorial and functional distribution of official authority across taxpayers and cases.

descriptors.concept_name: Civil Court Powers and Inquiry Authority of Tax Officials
descriptors.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
inclusion: Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.
